name: page_through_file_contents
description: Opens a window and shows a named file page by page, with a filename prompt, a percentage indicator and a More prompt, and it quits when the q key is pressed. It reports a window that cannot be opened, a file that may be binary, a file not found, and the end of file.

name: pass_global_words_to_routine
description: Calls another routine four times, passing a structure member from its argument together with each of four consecutive global array words in turn. It returns nothing.

name: validate_buffer_text_bytes
description: Calls a routine twice with buffer arguments derived from its input, then scans up to eighty bytes of the buffer. It returns zero when every byte is outside the rejected control-code ranges and the 128 to 159 range, and one at the first rejected byte.

name: dispatch_pager_key_command
description: Waits for input with a timeout, then reads one key and maps its code to an action such as paging, searching, moving or quitting. The recovered listing is truncated, so only the opening wait and the first part of the dispatch are certain.

name: call_two_routines_then_indirect
description: Calls one routine with a global variable, calls a second routine with no arguments, then calls through an address register and returns. The text shown in the facts is not used in this body.

name: initialize_scan_state_and_loop
description: Sets a counter field to one and a flag field to zero, stores the result of a library call in the structure, and calls a routine on it. It then repeats that routine while the counter is positive, a position value in a nested structure is below its limit and the flag remains zero.

name: combine_results_and_increment_counter
description: Calls one routine on a buffer in its argument, passes that result with the buffer to a second routine, and stores the final result in a field. When a flag field is zero it increments a short counter in a nested structure.

name: scan_line_and_mark_formfeed
description: Reads up to one hundred twenty-eight bytes through a library call and finds the first newline or form-feed character. A form feed is rewritten as a caret, the letter L and a newline, a flag is set, and the routine returns the number of bytes consumed.

name: show_page_lines_until_quit
description: Repeats a display pass up to a line count computed from its structure, printing table entries while the scroll position is within range, then shows the More prompt. It reads a key and quits when the key is q or Control-C.

name: run_search_pass_until_found
description: Chooses a search prompt from a flag, runs search passes while a counter remains positive, and stops when a pass reports a match. It returns one when a match is found and zero when the counter runs out.

name: run_sequence_and_return_result
description: Makes a fixed sequence of calls that prepares a block, runs one routine with the caller's arguments and then finishes the block, returning the result of that middle call. Nothing else is referenced.

name: call_pair_then_optional_single
description: Calls a routine with two arguments, then calls it again with the first argument alone when a short flag in the block is zero.

name: call_with_block_fields
description: Calls a routine with two fields from the block and the value minus one, then calls a second routine with a short field from a nested structure. It returns nothing.

name: call_pair_with_decremented_field
description: Calls a routine with the block's handle, zero and one, then calls a second routine with a short field from a nested structure minus one.

name: print_page_lines_from_buffer
description: Prints up to a set number of lines from a text buffer, scanning up to one hundred twenty-eight bytes at a time for newline and form-feed characters to count lines. It sets a flag at a form feed and uses library calls to position and write output.

name: forward_block_call_with_global
description: Calls a routine with the second argument, then calls a routine whose address is taken from a field of the block, passing a global value and the first argument. It returns nothing.

name: set_flag_and_forward
description: When a field in the block is zero it sets a short flag in a nested structure to one. It then calls a routine from the block with a global value.

name: dispatch_by_flag_argument
description: Calls a routine from a field of the block with a global value, passing a second argument that is either a global or a short field from a nested structure plus one, depending on a flag in the block.

name: dispatch_text_output_by_flag
description: Calls a routine from a field of the block with either three global references or a global reference and a short field from a nested structure, depending on a flag in the block. The text pattern for two strings is referenced.

name: clamp_negative_result
description: Calls a routine twice with the same first argument, once with zero and one and once with zero and minus one, then returns the second result with negative values clamped to zero.

name: copy_buffered_bytes_forward
description: Copies up to a requested number of bytes from a buffer region in the block to the destination, limited to the bytes still available. It then advances the buffer offset and reduces the remaining count, calling a routine to refill the buffer first when too few bytes remain, and returns the number of bytes moved.

name: refill_buffer_and_reset_offsets
description: Returns zero while the buffer is partly filled, and when it is full calls a routine to write out the buffered data. It then reads into the free space of a 4096-byte buffer, adds the count returned to the remaining count, resets the offset fields and returns that count.

name: update_viewport_position
description: Computes a target position from the offset argument, which is absolute, relative to the current position or relative to the end, and checks it against the visible window bounds. When the target is outside the window it moves the window through a routine call and updates its offset fields, returning the previous position, or minus one for an invalid mode.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Reads characters one at a time through a routine into a destination buffer until a newline or a limit of roughly 127 characters is reached. It then writes a zero terminator and returns the count of characters stored before it.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination until and including the zero terminator.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Walks a zero-terminated string and changes each lowercase letter from a to z to its uppercase form, leaving other bytes unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal_string
description: Converts a string to an integer by reading an optional plus or minus sign and then decimal digits, applying the sign to the result. The first character that is not a digit ends the conversion.

name: call_library_with_mask
description: When a pointer argument is nonzero and a field in the structure is set, calls the library routine held in that field with the pointer and minus one. It returns nothing.

name: process_entry_and_write_text
description: Processes an entry by calling routines on its linked fields, then writes either the given text or the entry's own text to its output handle. When the entry has its enabled flag set it reads characters until a newline, copies saved fields back into the entry and finishes with a final routine call.

name: pass_single_word_to_library
description: Stores its argument in a one-word stack buffer and passes it, with the constant 994 and a size of one, to a library function reached through a pointer from another routine's result. It returns the value that call produces.

name: copy_fields_from_allocated_block
description: Allocates a cleared 36-byte block and passes its shifted address with the constant 25 to a library function. It then copies two fields from the block into the caller's structure and frees the block, returning the library result, or zero when the allocation fails.

name: allocate_linked_node_with_words
description: Allocates a cleared 68-byte node, links it to a looked-up handle and copies a count of words from the source into it. It passes the node to a routine, releases the handle, and returns the node's stored value, or zero when a step fails.

description: Forwards its two arguments to a second routine together with the address of a stack slot, then returns. No text, library calls or constants are referenced.

name: read_one_signed_byte
description: Calls a routine with a small stack buffer and the count one, returning the byte as a signed value when one byte was transferred and minus one otherwise.

name: format_stack_text_and_emit
description: Calls exec's RawDoFmt to fill a 140-byte stack buffer, then measures the text up to its terminator and passes the text and its length to an output routine when the length is nonzero.

name: store_low_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in an address register. It is a single byte store with no other effect.

name: divide_longword_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a divisor, using bit-by-bit shift and subtract when the divisor exceeds 16 bits and two 16-bit divide steps otherwise. It returns the remainder and quotient together.

name: multiply_32bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products, returning the 32-bit product in its high part and the second operand with its halves swapped in its low part.

name: call_own_entry_then_return
description: Calls its own entry point with no arguments and then returns, with no other effect.

name: negate_result_on_flag
description: Calls a routine with no arguments and returns its result, negated when the second register value it leaves is nonzero.

name: invoke_exec_rawdofmt
description: Calls exec's RawDoFmt through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: store_low_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in an address register. It is a single byte store with no other effect.

name: invoke_library_vector_276
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 276 from it, with no arguments and no result.

name: create_message_port_with_signal
description: Allocates a signal bit, then a cleared 34-byte message port whose fields are set from the arguments, with the current task stored in it. It adds the port through a library call, and when allocation fails it frees the signal bit and returns zero.

name: delete_message_port_and_free
description: Removes a message port from the system when its link field is set, marks its status fields as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases its 34-byte memory block.

name: search_text_for_pattern
description: Searches text for a zero-terminated pattern one position at a time and returns one when the pattern is found. It gives up at a newline or the end of the text and returns zero.

name: initialize_empty_list_header
description: Initializes a list header in a block by storing the header's address plus four in its first word, clearing its second word and pointing its third word back at the header. It has no return value.

name: parse_args_and_open_handle
description: Allocates a message and task record and splits the argument text into tokens, expanding quoted strings and asterisk escapes. It opens a DOS file handle through dos.Open, stores it in the record and runs the shared cleanup routine before returning.

name: close_handles_and_reply
description: Stores its argument as the result in a message record, closes a DOS handle and a library when they are set, frees the record's memory, and replies to the message port with the stored result. The calls shown are dos.Close, exec.CloseLibrary, FreeMem, Forbid and ReplyMsg.

name: invoke_exec_allocmem
description: Calls exec's AllocMem function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_switch
description: Calls exec's Switch function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_forbid
description: Calls exec's Forbid function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_dispatch
description: Calls the exec Dispatch function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_schedule
description: Calls exec's Schedule function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_allocabs
description: Calls exec's AllocAbs function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: invoke_exec_reschedule
description: Calls exec's Reschedule function through the library base held in a global variable and returns nothing.

name: initialize_disk_from_arguments
description: Parses the DRIVE, NAME, FFS, NOICONS and QUICK keywords from the arguments and prints the usage text when they are missing. It prompts for a disk to be inserted and press return, reports a drive that is not found, and then runs the disk setup and icon steps through library calls.

name: release_stored_format_buffers
description: Releases up to five stored buffers in turn, passing each to a release routine together with its known size where one applies, and then calls a final routine with its argument.

name: map_disk_error_to_message
description: Reads a status code from a device call, retries while it reports a particular retry code, and maps the code to one of the messages for a bad sector, a device that cannot be opened, a changed disk, a seek error or a request to try a different disk. It prints the chosen message and returns the code as a short.

name: report_format_status_message
description: Prints a format status message, either a fixed pair of messages with a request or one message selected by a stored value, then returns the status byte. The texts for write protection, format errors and a missing disk are referenced.

name: match_value_in_table
description: Looks for the argument among eight bytes of a global table and stores the matching byte, or zero when none matches, into a field of a structure obtained through a routine. It returns the argument unchanged.

name: find_drive_entry_by_name
description: Walks a list of entries through a pointer chain, matching each entry whose flag field is zero either by a stored value or by a name argument. On a match it builds a drive label through two routines and returns one, or zero when the list ends.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Counts the bytes before the zero terminator of a string and returns that count.

name: copy_cstring_to_buffer
description: Copies a zero-terminated byte string from the source to the destination, including the terminator.

name: convert_char_to_uppercase
description: Returns the byte as an uppercase letter when it is a lowercase letter from a to z, and returns it unchanged otherwise.

name: compare_strings_ignoring_case
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings after converting each byte to uppercase. It returns one when they are identical through the terminator and zero at the first difference.

name: cut_string_at_colon
description: Terminates a string at its first colon, or at its existing terminator when no colon is present.

name: call_single_argument_with_code
description: Passes its first argument, as a one-element stack array with a count of one, to a routine together with the constant 31. It returns 126 when that routine reports failure and zero otherwise.

name: allocate_node_limited_words
description: Allocates a cleared 68-byte node, links it to a looked-up handle and copies up to seven words from the source into it. It passes the node to a routine, releases the handle, and returns the node's stored value, or zero when a step fails.

name: format_disk_tracks_with_progress
description: Opens the disk device, reads its geometry, and writes each track in turn, reporting progress with the labels Formatting, Initializing disk and Verifying and the cylinder count. The recovered listing is truncated, so the later steps are not certain.
